title: Mt.FUJI 100 — RULES & REGULATIONS (競技規則・注意事項)
claims: Two cut-off times are set at each aid station, one at the entrance and one at the exit, and a runner who does not enter and leave by the respective times is disqualified.

A runner who leaves an aid station may return to it before the entrance cut-off time, but must use the designated passage, inform staff and leave again before the exit cut-off time or be disqualified.

Cut-off times may change depending on weather, course conditions and race progress, and any change is announced on the official bulletin board at the aid station and by email to the registered mobile phone.

The use of poles is prohibited on the whole FUJI100mi course except from F5 onwards; poles must be stored in a drop bag beforehand, tree branches may not be used as substitutes, and once a runner has poles they must keep them to the finish.
Pole use on the FUJI100mi is described as experimental, with future permission to be decided from the monitoring results, and pole-free zones remain even after F5, mainly inside the national park.
Sleeping on the course is prohibited because of its impact on the natural environment and because a sleeping runner may be mistaken for someone needing emergency help.
Leaving the trail, including cutting corners, is prohibited, and no-overtaking restrictions apply in areas where the natural environment needs protection.

As a general rule, participants are not allowed to retire at the F7/K3 Nijumagari Pass, where a retiring runner may have to wait a long time and supporters, friends and family are not allowed to pick them up by car.
Total equipment must exceed 2 kg at the start and when leaving any aid station, and must never fall below 1 kg anywhere on the course; missing mandatory items can lead to immediate disqualification.

The mandatory list has 19 items for the Mt.FUJI100/KAI70k, including two lights of at least 80 lumens and at least 4 hours of burn time with spare batteries for each, a cup of at least 150 cc, at least 1 litre of water when leaving the start and each aid station, food, a survival blanket of at least 130 cm by 200 cm, a whistle, taping tape, a portable toilet, a hooded rain jacket and rain trousers, a fleece or similar long-sleeved top, leg cover to the ankle, gloves and a hat covering the ears, a first-aid kit, the number card and IC chip, a pack, and a power bank capable of charging the phone.

The organisers aim to reach a runner who cannot move within 3 hours of a call, but in the FUJI100mi and KAI70k it can take 6 hours or more, and runners are told to choose equipment on the assumption of waiting on course for 6 hours in cold wind or freezing rain.
Each runner must wear an IC chip on each shoe, and runners who withdraw or are disqualified must return the chip at the retirement desk of each aid station.

Doctors and rescuers have the authority to stop a runner who cannot continue, and a runner still near a checkpoint after the checkpoint time, including the finish time, may be stopped and asked to return to their vehicle.

The rules page gives Lake Yamanaka (992 m) hourly weather for 25 April aggregated over 2022-2026: temperature averages 7.5 to 17.0 C with a minimum of 0.1 C and a maximum of 21.9 C, wind averages 0.3 to 2.8 m/s with a maximum of 4.3 m/s, and precipitation averages of 0 to 0.1 mm.
The rules page states that most of the course lies between 500 m and 1,600 m of altitude.

If pregnancy is confirmed between entry and the race, the entry fee is fully refunded and the runner's eligibility is maintained for two years; runners returning after childbirth may be recognised on performances from before pregnancy within three years of returning.

The race follows the ITRA Green Charter, prohibits littering and collecting plants, animals, fungi or rocks, asks runners to carry out toilet paper, to use toilets at aid stations, and to start with clean-soled shoes to avoid introducing invasive species.
Even without a safety problem on the day, the organisers may create walking sections, change the course or cancel the event if the trail cannot support a large number of participants.

claimVerification.note: 第7节：'関門時刻はエイドステーションの入口と出口のふたつ'；未通过则失格
第7节第 2 条：出站后可在入口关门前返回，需走指定通道并告知工作人员
第7节第 3 条：天候、コース状況、レース進行により変更；エイドの掲示板と登録携帯へのメールで通知
第2节：'F5 以降を除きポール使用禁止'；事前にドロップバッグへ；木の枝等の代用禁止；一度所持したらフィニッシュまで
第2节括注：試験的運用、モニタリング結果で今後判断；F5 以降も国立公園内中心に禁止区間
第2节：'コース上での睡眠は禁止'，理由为环境影响与可能被误认为需要救助
第2节：ショートカット等のコース逸脱禁止；自然保護上必要な区域では追い越し禁止
第6节：'原則として F7/K3 二十曲峠でのリタイアは不可'；第9节：迎えの車不可、長時間待つ場合あり
第10节：装備総量 スタート時・各エイド出発時 2kg 超、コース上常時 1kg 未満不可；欠品はその場で失格の可能性
第10节必携品表 19 项：ライト 80ルーメン以上4時間以上×2＋予備電池、携帯コップ150cc以上、水1ℓ以上、サバイバルブランケット130×200cm、ホイッスル、テーピングテープ、携帯トイレ、レインジャケット／パンツ、フリース等長袖、足首までズボン／タイツ、手袋・耳まで帽子、ファーストエイドキット、ナンバーカード・ICチップ、ザック、モバイルバッテリー等
第10节注：連絡から3時間以内到着を目指すが、FUJI100mi/KAI70k では6時間以上かかることもある
第6节：ICチップは両足のシューズに装着；リタイア／失格時は各エイドのリタイアデスクへ返却
第5节：医師・救助隊に停止権限；関門時刻後も近くにいる場合停止し車両へ戻すことがある
气象表下注：'コースの大部分が標高500m～1600mの間'
第3节：妊娠延期制度，全额退款并保留资格两年；产后复归按孕前成绩认定（复归三年内）
第2节：ITRA Green Charter、垃圾与采集禁止、厕纸带走、清洁鞋底
第2节末：可设步行区间、改线或取消
